name: Brus Denmark
description: Brus Denmark is a partnership or solo trick-taking game from the Karnöffel family in which special beating cards, sevens and certain kings outrank the rest of the deck. Players aim to win five tricks out of nine and can score bonus points by "risking" high honours that may be beaten.
deck: 36 cards (French pack: 6–10, J, Q, K, A in each suit)

history.origins: Brus descends from the German game Brusbart in the wider Karnöffel family and was historically a rural West Jutland game. It spread through Denmark and to Swedish-speaking communities in Estonia while retaining the family’s distinctive matadors and special sevens.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

rules.objective: Be the first player to achieve the winning condition through strategic play of cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. Setup: prepare players, deck or tiles, and opening layout according to the variant. 2. Turn loop: each player performs one legal action (play, capture, build, bet, or pass/draw as applicable). 3. Resolution: each action updates control of tricks/cards/pot/layout. 4. End condition: when hand-ending criteria are met, scoring is computed and match state advances.
keyRules: Play proceeds in turn order with only legal actions allowed.
Round resolution follows the variant's scoring and bonus conditions.
Match winner is determined by agreed target score or elimination condition.

strategy.basic: Brus Denmark: follow rules; strategy depends on variant.
strategy.intermediate: Track revealed information (cards, tiles, tricks, or betting patterns) and adjust plan as opponent ranges narrow.

tips: Fix the exact local variant before play so edge cases are predictable.
Plan two turns ahead: most mistakes come from giving opponents forced value.
Recalculate risk near end-of-hand scoring thresholds.

variations.name: Brus with 4-card hands
variations.description: Variant where each player is dealt four cards instead of three, making it possible to lead four cards together and increasing the frequency of multiple-card tricks while keeping the same beating-card structure.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Engine-level overrides for hand size and multiple-trick handling are not yet modelled; base rules still describe the standard 3-card version.

variations.name: Brus with no stock
variations.description: All cards are dealt at the start of the hand (for example 9 each in the four-player partnership game), so there is no stock to draw from and every trick is played from a fixed hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Full engine overrides for the all-cards-dealt (no stock) variant are pending; rules text documents the structure but engine uses the standard stock-based form.

scoring.description: Score points by winning the hand (taking the majority of tricks) and by successfully risking or smacking high honours such as Brus and Galhund; points are tracked as sticks or strokes erased from a shared comb.
scoring.winCondition: First team or player to discard all of their sticks or erase all strokes on their side of the comb wins the game.

synthesis.shortDescription: Brus Denmark is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.
